title: Residue field extensions of a finite group action are normal, and the decomposition group surjects onto the automorphism group
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The statement concerns a finite group acting on a ring and a prime lying over a prime of the invariant subring, and asserts first that the residue field extension is algebraic normal and then that the decomposition group maps onto its automorphism group (statement lines 32703-32716). The proof first reduces to the case where the prime below is maximal, which keeps the decomposition group and the residue fields unchanged, then exploits the single orbit of the primes over it: an element vanishing at all the other primes is chosen through the Chinese remainder theorem, the product of its translates splits completely and forces the required minimal polynomial to split, and the same element is reused after splitting the extension into a purely inseparable and a Galois part to realize every Galois conjugate by a translate under the decomposition group, the infinite case being excluded by a degree count (proof lines 32718-32773). The union of the normality argument and the conjugate realization is what makes the surjectivity statement work. The counted span refers seven times, twice to results of this chapter and five times to results of other chapters, all carried as navigation stubs.
